Decide whether given facts are statistics

body.en: Bowley: "Statistics may be called the science of counting" and "the science of averages". Croxton and Cowden: "Statistics may be defined as the collection, presentation, analysis and interpretation of numerical data." R. A. Fisher saw statistics as mathematics applied to observational data. The Croxton and Cowden definition (singular sense) names the four stages of every statistical study.
body.kn: ಬೌಲೆ: "ಸಂಖ್ಯಾಶಾಸ್ತ್ರ ಎಣಿಕೆಯ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನ", "ಸರಾಸರಿಗಳ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನ". ಕ್ರಾಕ್ಸ್‌ಟನ್ ಮತ್ತು ಕೌಡೆನ್: "ಸಂಖ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕ ದತ್ತಾಂಶದ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಣೆ, ನಿರೂಪಣೆ, ವಿಶ್ಲೇಷಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ವ್ಯಾಖ್ಯಾನ" ಸಂಖ್ಯಾಶಾಸ್ತ್ರ. ಇದು ನಾಲ್ಕು ಹಂತಗಳನ್ನು ಹೆಸರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: Four stages of a statistical study

say.en: Croxton and Cowden give four stages. First we collect the data.
Then we present them in tables and diagrams, and analyse them with averages.
Last, we interpret: we draw a conclusion and act on it.
Secrist's test: one figure is not statistics; an aggregate is.

narration.en: On the board: Four stages of a statistical study.

body.en: Secrist defined statistics (plural sense) as "aggregates of facts, affected to a marked extent by a multiplicity of causes, numerically expressed, enumerated or estimated according to reasonable standards of accuracy, collected in a systematic manner for a predetermined purpose and placed in relation to each other." So statistics are: aggregates, affected by many causes, numerical, reasonably accurate, systematically collected, for a purpose fixed in advance, and comparable.
body.kn: ಸೆಕ್ರಿಸ್ಟ್ ಪ್ರಕಾರ ಅಂಕಿಅಂಶಗಳು: ಸಂಗತಿಗಳ ಸಮೂಹ, ಅನೇಕ ಕಾರಣಗಳಿಂದ ಪ್ರಭಾವಿತ, ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ವ್ಯಕ್ತ, ಯುಕ್ತ ನಿಖರತೆಯಿಂದ ಎಣಿಸಿದ ಅಥವಾ ಅಂದಾಜಿಸಿದ, ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥಿತವಾಗಿ ಮೊದಲೇ ನಿರ್ಧರಿಸಿದ ಉದ್ದೇಶಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸಿದ ಮತ್ತು ಹೋಲಿಸಬಹುದಾದ.

problem.en: Which of these are statistics? (a) Ravi's height is 165 cm. (b) The heights of 50 students of a class. (c) Mysuru is a beautiful city. (d) The populations of Karnataka's districts in Census 2011.

steps.en: (a) is a single, isolated fact: not an aggregate.
(c) is a qualitative remark, not numerically expressed.
(b) and (d) are aggregates of numerical facts, collected for a purpose and comparable.
